title: PMI CAPM (Certified Associate in Project Management) Study Guide
description: The Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM) is PMI's entry-level project management credential and requires no project experience. The exam is 150 questions in 180 minutes, of which 135 are scored, and it covers predictive project management, agile principles and frameworks, and business analysis — PMI's vocabulary applied to scenarios rather than definitions recited back.
audience: Career changers moving into project coordination, team members who run projects without the title, and students or recent graduates who want PMI recognition before they qualify for the PMP. The requirements are genuinely light: a secondary degree such as a high school diploma or global equivalent, at least 18 years old, and 23 hours of project management education completed before you sit — which PMI's own prep course, or a PMI-authorised course, satisfies outright.
why_get_it: CAPM matters because the PMP — the certification most people actually want — is not an entry-level credential: it requires 36+ months of documented project leadership experience. CAPM is PMI's answer for everyone earlier in the pipeline. It gets 'PMI-certified' onto a resume with no experience requirement, which helps entry candidates pass HR filters for project coordinator, project analyst, and PMO assistant roles. The 2023 exam overhaul made it more relevant than it used to be: agile frameworks (20%) and business analysis (27%) now make up nearly half the exam, so it maps to how modern teams actually work rather than pure waterfall theory. It also front-loads PMP preparation — the terminology, process logic, and PMI mindset transfer directly when you later qualify for PMP. Be realistic: CAPM is a door-opener and a signal of seriousness, not a role guarantee. It works best paired with any hands-on coordination experience you can point to, even informal.
when_to_get_it: Take CAPM when you want PMI's name on your resume but do not yet have the 36 months of project experience the PMP demands — that gap is the whole reason CAPM exists. It is worth most in industries where PMI credentials are the hiring filter: construction, healthcare, government, defence and large enterprises. In tech, agile and Scrum credentials often carry more weight for the same money. Knock out the 23 education hours first; the Google Project Management certificate alone banks over 100 hours, far more than CAPM asks for. And note the retake economics — three attempts a year, each at full price.
salary_note: Honest framing: CAPM by itself does not command a large salary premium — it is a resume signal, not a pay lever. Project coordinator and junior PM roles that list CAPM typically pay $55K–$80K in the US depending on industry and market; surveys put certified holders roughly 5–10% above uncertified peers at entry level. The real compensation jump comes later with experience and the PMP, where $100K+ is common. Treat CAPM as an investment in getting the first role, not in raising its pay.
exam_format: 150 questions in 180 minutes — 135 scored plus 15 unscored pretest items — multiple choice and multiple response, at a Pearson VUE test centre or online proctored, with an optional break at the midpoint. Offered in eleven languages. You may attempt the exam up to three times in one year.
recertification_note: CAPM is valid for three years and renews through PMI's Continuing Certification Requirements programme: earn 15 PDUs per three-year cycle, including a minimum of 2 PDUs in each area of the PMI Talent Triangle, and pay the renewal fee. This replaced the old rule under which CAPM expired after five years and required a full retake — you no longer re-sit the exam. Confirm current PDU rules and renewal fees on PMI's site.

skills_covered.category: Project Management Fundamentals and Core Concepts (36%)
items: Project life cycles, processes, and the role of the project manager
Core terminology: scope, schedule, cost, quality, risk, stakeholders
Organizational structures and project governance
Planning fundamentals and baseline concepts
Problem-solving and how projects deliver business value
When a predictive (waterfall) approach is appropriate
Work breakdown structures and scope decomposition
Schedule development: critical path, dependencies, milestones
Budgeting, estimating, and earned value basics
Change control in plan-driven projects
When adaptive approaches fit better than predictive
Scrum roles, events, and artifacts
Backlogs, iterations, and incremental delivery
Agile planning: story points, velocity, burn charts
Servant leadership and self-organizing teams
The business analyst role and how it interacts with project teams
Requirements gathering, elicitation, and traceability
Stakeholder communication and engagement
Product roadmaps and their influence on delivery
Validating requirements against business value

study_steps.title: Confirm eligibility and plan your 23 contact hours
study_steps.description: CAPM requires a secondary degree plus 23 contact hours of project management education completed before you sit the exam. Plan the contact hours first because most good prep courses satisfy the requirement while teaching the material — one purchase covers both. The Google Project Management Certificate, PM PrepCast, and the major Udemy CAPM courses all count.

study_steps.title: Download the CAPM Exam Content Outline
study_steps.description: Get the official Exam Content Outline (ECO) PDF from PMI. The 2023-onward exam is four domains: Fundamentals (36%), Predictive (17%), Agile (20%), and Business Analysis (27%). Note what that means: agile plus business analysis is nearly half the exam. If your study materials are waterfall-only leftovers from the old exam, they will fail you.

study_steps.title: Complete one primary course end to end
study_steps.description: Pick a single comprehensive course and finish it. Joseph Phillips and Andrew Ramdayal on Udemy are the most popular paid options and both include enough contact hours for eligibility. The Google Project Management Certificate on Coursera is a solid alternative that doubles as its own resume line. Do not stack multiple full courses — it slows you down without improving retention.

study_steps.title: Learn the vocabulary cold
study_steps.description: CAPM is heavily terminology-driven: process groups, Scrum events, requirement types, estimation techniques. Flash cards (Anki or Quizlet) work well here. PMI members get free digital access to the PMBOK Guide and Agile Practice Guide — worth joining before you study, since membership also discounts the exam by more than it costs if you qualify for student pricing.

study_steps.title: Drill practice questions across all four domains
study_steps.description: Work practice question banks until you consistently score 75–80% across every domain, not just overall. Candidates from IT backgrounds routinely under-prepare the business analysis domain (27% of the exam) because it feels unfamiliar — check your per-domain scores and attack the weakest one. PMI's official Study Hall is the closest match to real question style.

study_steps.title: Apply through PMI and schedule with Pearson VUE
study_steps.description: Submit your application on pmi.org documenting your education and contact hours. Join PMI first if the math works: membership ($139/year, or $32 for students) drops the exam fee from $300 to $225 and includes the PMBOK Guide. Once approved, schedule through Pearson VUE — online proctored or test center.

study_steps.title: Sit the exam with a pacing plan
study_steps.description: 150 questions in 180 minutes is a comfortable pace, but do not linger: flag hard questions and return to them. Take the optional 10-minute break at the midpoint — you cannot revisit earlier questions after it, so review flagged items first. Read scenario questions for the approach being described (predictive vs agile) before picking an answer; that framing decides many questions.

voucher_links.label: Apply for the CAPM Exam – PMI.org
voucher_links.note: PMI does not sell vouchers through resellers — you apply and pay on pmi.org, and the fee is shown during the application, at member and non-member rates. Check whether you qualify for student membership before you apply: where the member discount exceeds the dues, joining first is simply cheaper. Confirm the current fee on PMI's site or in the CAPM Exam Content Outline before budgeting.

faq.question: Is CAPM worth it?
faq.answer: It depends on where you are. For candidates with no project experience targeting coordinator, analyst, or PMO roles, yes — it is the recognized entry credential from the organization whose PMP dominates the field, and it helps pass resume filters. For anyone with 3+ years leading projects, no — go straight to the PMP. CAPM is a door-opener, not a career-maker; pair it with any real coordination experience you can demonstrate.

faq.question: CAPM vs PMP — which should I get?
faq.answer: This is decided for you by eligibility. The PMP requires 36+ months of project leadership experience; if you have that, get the PMP — it carries far more weight. If you do not, the PMP is simply unavailable and CAPM is PMI's credential for you. CAPM is not a prerequisite for the PMP and does not waive any PMP requirements, but the material overlaps heavily, so the study effort transfers.

faq.question: What are the CAPM prerequisites?
faq.answer: A secondary degree (high school diploma, GED, or global equivalent) and 23 contact hours of project management education completed before you take the exam. PMI removed the old 1,500-hour experience alternative in 2024, so the education route is now the only path. Most prep courses — Udemy's major CAPM courses, PM PrepCast, and the Google Project Management Certificate — satisfy the contact hours.

faq.question: How hard is the CAPM exam?
faq.answer: It is the easiest PMI exam, but not free: 150 questions in 3 hours across four domains, and the 2023 overhaul added agile (20%) and business analysis (27%) content that trips up candidates studying from outdated waterfall-only material. PMI does not publish a numeric passing score — results are scored psychometrically and reported as proficiency levels. Most candidates prepare in 4 to 8 weeks part-time.

faq.question: How much does the CAPM cost?
faq.answer: The exam is $225 for PMI members and $300 for non-members (verify current pricing on pmi.org). PMI membership is $139/year plus a $10 application fee — or $32/year for students, which makes membership clearly worth it since the member discount is $75. Retakes are ~$150 for members / ~$200 for non-members. Add a prep course and total cost typically lands between $350 and $600.

faq.question: Does the CAPM expire?
faq.answer: Yes — CAPM is valid for 3 years and renews through PMI's CCR program: 15 PDUs per cycle (minimum 2 in each Talent Triangle area) plus a renewal fee (~$60 members / ~$150 non-members). This replaced the old five-year expiration that forced a full exam retake. PDUs are easy to earn through free webinars and PMI content, so renewal is low-effort if you stay engaged.

faq.question: What jobs can I get with CAPM?
faq.answer: Project Coordinator, Project Analyst, PMO Assistant/Analyst, Junior Project Manager, and IT coordinator roles that carry project duties. Business analysts also use it to formalize project management skills. Be realistic: most listings for these roles ask for the cert or experience, not the cert alone — CAPM strengthens an application, it does not replace internships, portfolio work, or demonstrated coordination experience.
